# SSH-010: sshd listens where it is configured to

- **Group:** SSH
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

On Ubuntu 22.10 and later sshd is socket activated: ssh.socket opens the listening sockets, generated from Port and ListenAddress only on daemon-reload. Changing the port in sshd_config without a reload and a socket restart leaves the old port open and the new one closed, so firewall rules, fail2ban jails and the admin's belief no longer match reality. Socket activation by itself is not a finding: when ssh.socket listens exactly where Port and ListenAddress say (or, with no ListenAddress set, on the configured port, leaving the addresses to the socket), the check passes. It warns when the socket listens somewhere the config does not name or ignores a ListenAddress, and fails when a configured address or port has no listener.

## Verify by hand

```sh
sudo sshd -T | grep -Ei '^(port|listenaddress)'; ss -tln; systemctl status ssh.socket
```

## How to fix it

systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart ssh.socket (or restart ssh.service without socket activation), then compare ss -tln with sshd -T again.

## What a fix can break

Restarting the socket moves the listener: keep the current session open and test a new login on the new port before closing it.
